items.heading: In the Us, Mortuary Science
items.text: In the US, mortuary science is a real, formal field: dedicated associate and bachelor's degree programmes, a national licensing exam, and a licensed funeral-director or embalmer credential that a graduate can build a career and even a private funeral-home business around. Nothing equivalent exists in India today.

items.heading: Most People Who Search "Mortuary
items.text: Most people who search "mortuary science careers in India" have seen the concept somewhere specifically American: a US crime show, a YouTube video about a mortuary science degree, or a Reddit thread about becoming a mortician. That search intent quietly assumes an Indian structure that mirrors the American one, a college programme, a licensing exam, a title, a typical salary.

items.heading: Four Distinct Things Exist
items.text: Four distinct things exist in this general space in India, and conflating them is where most of the confusion starts.

rows: Performing legal post-mortems, determining cause of death, medico-legal certification, and courtroom testimony as a qualified doctor.
Analysing biological, digital, chemical, or documentary evidence in a lab setting, across eight distinct specialisations.
NEET-UG, MBBS, internship, then NEET-PG for an MD/MS/DNB seat in Forensic Medicine, a genuine two-step competitive path.
A science-stream 12th, then a BSc/MSc in forensic science (NFSU or another recognised university), plus a state or central recruitment exam for a government lab seat.

Follows the government doctor pay scale, which sits well above most other roles discussed on this page, plus a real but modest private stream: medico-legal consultancy, insurance case reviews, and expert-witness fees tied to reputation.

Government FSL tracks (biology, toxicology, ballistics, documents) follow a fixed government scale; digital forensics and forensic accounting, two of the eight tracks, currently pay noticeably more because they sit mostly in the private sector.
Roughly 9-10 years end to end: MBBS plus internship, then a 3-year postgraduate specialisation, before a candidate is a practising forensic medicine specialist.
Roughly 3-5 years: a BSc or integrated BSc-MSc, followed by exam preparation for a government lab seat, or a certification-led route into digital forensics or forensic accounting.

items.heading: You Are Drawn to Determining
items.text: You are drawn to determining cause of death and standing behind that finding in court, not to preparing or presenting a body.

items.heading: You Are Genuinely Prepared
items.text: You are genuinely prepared to clear NEET-UG and NEET-PG, two separate competitive step, roughly a decade apart from start to specialisation.

items.heading: You Want the Highest Real
items.text: You want the highest real income ceiling of the options on this page, built on a government doctor's pay scale.
